text.p: Following are the top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- It is "mere wishful thinking" on the part of Beijing to want to impose the "one country, two systems" model of reunification on Taiwan, says the island's President, Mr Lee Teng-hui, adding that "nothing good will come out of one side forcing its will on the other".
- Motorists turning left at 25 junctions islandwide will not have to stop for the red traffic light under a scheme to cut their waiting time.

- Black smoke fills the public concourse at Subang international airport in Malaysia, raising fears of a fire that led to panic among passengers at Terminal One before the discovery that it was a false alarm.
- Singapore security system companies enjoy a boost in business as landed property owners react to recent spate of armed robberies by beefing up security.

- Three members of Jumabhoy family who are Scotts Holdings directors are banned from being directors of other listed companies as their disputes have detracted them from their primary duty to the company, Stock Exchange of Singapore says.
- Singapore banks react to fall in value of Thai currency by cutting interest rates for baht deposits.

- DBS Bank may make further inroads into Thailand's financial sector, having received regulatory approval to increase its 10 percent shareholding in listed Sri Dhana Finance Co to majority 60 percent stake.
- Thailand's stocks surge by another 8.6 percent, bringing gains in last two days to 17.2 percent, buoyed by expectations the devaluation of baht would revive ailing economy.
- Hong Kong market starts first trading day under Chinese sovereignty on generally weak note with property counters hit by Chief Executive Tung Chee-hwa's pledge to tackle housing shortage.
- More charges expected to be levelled against various CAM International Holdings parties by Commercial Affairs Department.
- Singapore-listed Singatronics almost certain to let the Le Meridien Hotel chain manage Singapore $130 million hotel it is developing in Sydney.
- Injection mould-maker Li Xin Industries gearing up for listing on mainboard of Stock Exchange of Singapore in year or so.
